TSLA.reasoning:
Vote tally: 4 neutral (trend_momentum 30, mean_reversion 30, breakout 72, macro_context 38), 1 bearish (catalyst_news 58), 0 bullish. Consensus is neutral with a soft bearish lean. The neutral bloc is NOT a bullish disagreement — every neutral agent explicitly says 'wait for a better entry.' No agent is buying here.

Price at $392.51 sits squarely inside the $387–$399 bear-rally resistance cluster documented with 14–15 prior tests. This is the same price zone that produced 4 consecutive holds across 5 prior TSLA runs (Apr 11, Apr 17, May 1, May 4) — that consistency is itself a signal. The model has never found a clean entry in this zone, and today's data does not change that picture.

The most actionable directional call comes from catalyst_news: the Kevin Warsh Fed Chair Senate confirmation vote on May 15 (~7 trading days) is a hawkish macro headwind for high-valuation, high-beta growth names like TSLA (P/E stretched, DCF gap -97%). A hawkish Fed Chair signal compresses multiples on exactly this type of name. This catalyst is time-bound, specific, and not yet fully priced. macro_context corroborates the Warsh risk and confirms the R/R at current price fails the 2:1 minimum (1.26:1 to nearest resistance target at $409.28 from $379 stop).

Breakout agent has the highest single-agent confidence (72) but is explicitly a 'watch-not-act' verdict — it requires a confirmed daily close above $409.28 on 1.5x+ volume (gate not met; current volume 0.74x) or a close below $381.40 for a bearish breakdown trade. Neither trigger has fired.

Wiki memory dials confidence further down: (a) The one closed trade in lessons.md is an EMA pullback Fib dip-buy on NVDA that stopped out at -$63.20 with 0% win rate — this is structurally identical to the conditional long scenario that trend_momentum and mean_reversion both propose (buy dip to $381–$385). That setup-type has a negative P&L track record. (b) TSLA trade history: 0 fills ever, 5 consecutive holds, all from the same $387–$399 zone. Adding a position here would break with a consistent, reasoned pattern.

Open positions book: 3 longs, 3 shorts — net flat. No stacking concern in either direction, but no urgency to add exposure.

Hourly OBV is diverging bearishly from price (flagged independently by 4 of 5 agents) — this distribution signal is the most cross-confirmed technical read in the entire dataset. It suggests larger players are selling into the $370→$392 post-earnings relief rally.

Strategic web research (provided externally) adds nuance: structural TSLA positives (EU FSD pathway, Tesla Semi, Terafab foundry) are multi-month catalysts already priced into the +6% earnings move. Near-term negatives are more actionable — Warsh vote, $573M related-party governance concerns, record Q1 inventory gap (50,363 unsold vehicles), analyst consensus PT at $400–$406 leaving minimal upside from $392. Analyst consensus is Hold, not Buy.

Conditional watch levels: LONG entry if price pulls back to $381–$385 on declining volume with a bullish daily reversal candle (R/R ~3:1 from that zone to $409.28, stop below $374). SHORT entry if price breaks and closes below $381.40 on above-average volume (Warsh catalyst + technical breakdown confluence). Neither condition is met today.
TSLA.key_conflicts: The primary conflict is between catalyst_news (bearish, 58 confidence) and the four neutral agents. catalyst_news argues the Warsh Fed Chair vote May 15 is a near-term directional catalyst warranting a short entry now ($393.50 → $381.40, ~2.5:1 R/R). The four neutral agents — trend_momentum, mean_reversion, breakout, and macro_context — collectively say the R/R at current price fails the 2:1 minimum and that no entry condition has been met yet. This is not a bullish-vs-bearish split; it is 'act now on the Warsh catalyst' vs 'wait for a cleaner entry level.' The disagreement is telling: the Warsh event is real and bearish, but the reward-to-risk from $392.51 is marginal (~2.5:1 on catalyst_news's short, vs the <1.3:1 the macro_context calculates to nearer targets). A secondary conflict: trend_momentum's conditional long at $381 (buy-the-dip EMA thesis) directly contradicts catalyst_news's short thesis. trend_momentum and catalyst_news are pointing in opposite directions at the same $381 price level — trend_momentum wants to buy there, catalyst_news wants the breakdown below it as a short confirmation. Resolution: the one closed lesson (EMA dip-buy = -$63.20, 0% win rate) and the wiki's repeated 'watch-not-act' across 5 TSLA runs argue against the trend_momentum conditional long. The breakout agent's high confidence (72) is deceptive — it is not bullish, it is a 'no active setup' verdict with defined triggers that have not fired. Hourly OBV bearish divergence, flagged by 4 of 5 agents independently, is the strongest cross-confirmed signal in the dataset and directionally supports the catalyst_news bearish lean — but it is not sufficient alone to override the failed R/R math at current price.
